svg.data-depth-with-brackets: 782 mm over cable-management brackets, air filter and handles (Table 22)
svg.data-throughput: 4.8 Tbps system capacity; up to 12x400 Gbps or 48x100 Gbps ports (three LMICs)
svg.data-storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C in shipping container
svg.data-asic: Juniper Trio 6 (one YT ASIC per LMIC)
svg.data-macsec: inline MACsec on all ports at all speeds
svg.data-timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB input and output, ToD and BITS RJ45, GM/PTP SFP (1-GbE/10-GbE); BITS and GM/PTP currently reserved for future use per the guide
svg.data-redundancy: full hardware redundancy - Routing Engines, power supplies and fans

Positions are photo-fractions, approximate"},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet-table - Table 22: chassis 3.5 x 17.36 x 24.01 in (88.9 x 440.8 x 610 mm), 2RU; 78.2 cm deep over cable-management brackets and handles. The chassis-description prose says 17.63 in (44.8 cm) wide - a 0.7 cm disagreement with Table 22; the table is carried and the prose recorded here. Fully loaded 32 kg, bare 16 kg. Ears are NOT MODELLED by project convention; the modelled body is the 440.8 mm between the flange folds, and the slot labels (RE 0, LMIC0, RE1/LMIC2, LMIC1) are printed on the REMOVABLE BRACKETS the photographs show, so they appear nowhere on this body - recorded so their absence is not read as an omission"},"color":{"note":"photo - medium grey chassis (#8b8f94), bright aluminium module plates, pale blue ejector levers, Juniper orange fan furniture"},"esd":{"note":"guide Figure 11 (ESD Points) - one point on the front badge strip top, one on the rear right above the earthing plate. Absence of the announcement is the finding"},"other-faces":{"note":"near-blank by evidence - no source shows the top, bottom or side faces; each carries only an estimated mounting-rail band so the capability chain counts it as drawn, sized from Table 22. Axis conventions per viewer3d.js: LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, top and bottom y = 0 at the FRONT"},"power":{"note":"guide Table 25, the vendor's own per-module table at two ambients for the 3.2 Tbps two-RE + two-LMIC 100GbE configuration: REs 49/59 W each, SFB+CB+PMB 155/228 (chassis internals, not a FRU here), LMICs 318/410 each with transceivers, fans 48/90 each; total chassis power 1033 W at 25 C and 1436 W at 46 C. Those totals are carried as the device figures with that scope in power-envelope; Table 26 gives the 400GbE configuration and its totals fell outside this extraction's text layer - not carried rather than guessed"},"rear":{"note":"photo (mx304-rear-ac-high) - stacked PSU bays at x 10.9 (PSU 0 above PSU 1, labels printed vertically on the chassis strip right of them), the fixed timing strip at 84-116, three 82.0 mm fan bays EVENLY spaced at x 116.4, 225.4 and 334.5 (26.9 mm label strips between and after, each printing the bay's number, lamp and fan icon), and the earthing plate and rear ESD socket at the right end. A FIRST READING PUT FAN 1 AT 213.4 AND CALLED THE SPACING ASYMMETRIC - it had mis-assigned fan 1's edges to its grille internals; the DC rear photograph (independent shot, same chassis) and a zoom on the strip between fans 1 and 2 both give the even layout, and the reviewer's instinct that routers do not stagger their fans was what triggered the re-measure. The rear drawing (g101368 family) was measured too but its verticals mix module internals at this threshold and were not used for positions"},"scale":{"note":"photo + drawing, cross-anchored per axis - the guide front drawing (g101366) measures aspect 5.58 against the rack face's 5.43 and is internally inconsistent in x by ~1.5%, and the front photograph is ~16% COMPRESSED in y (near-axis studio shot) while consistent in x. So: front x positions come from the photograph at 4.058 px/mm anchored to the 440.8 body, front y positions from the drawing anchored to the 88.9 height. The rear photograph is near-isotropic (3%) and rear positions come from it at 4.236 px/mm (x) / 4.106 (y). Feature sizes come from the registry and Table 22 throughout"},"slots":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing + photo - four half-width apertures in two columns of two: RE 0 above LMIC 0 on the left, RE 1/LMIC2 above LMIC 1 on the right (guide Figure 2 callouts name all four). Rows y 4.1-43.8 and 44.6-84.3 off the drawing; columns x 1.2-198.8 and 205.3-402.9 off the photograph, separated by the centre rail. A one-RE system may seat a THIRD LMIC in the RE 1/LMIC2 slot (guide Figure 3 shows it; hardware overview text: \"You can also add a third LMIC into one of the Routing Engine slots\"). The 197.6 mm apertures take 203.5 mm module envelopes - the modules carry insert: for the difference"},"sources":{"note":"MX304 Universal Routing Platform Hardware Guide (figures g101366/ g101368/g101334/g101624 among others), MX304 datasheet (mx304-datasheet.pdf), Juniper image-library studio photographs mx304-front-high, mx304-rear-ac-high and mx304-rear-dc-high, and the NetBox devicetype-library MX304 elevations.
